title: The gateway's outcome split has FOUR states, and `unknown` is not a success
summary: `usage.outcome` returns delivered / hollow / failed / unknown as four mutually exclusive states that sum to `total`. `unknown` means the row predates the `output_chars` column, so the split cannot be computed for it — it is 'we cannot tell', not 'it worked'. An agent that folds unknown into delivered produces a false all-clear, which is the exact class of confidently-wrong number this surface was rebuilt to remove: before the rebuild, `agent/chat` reported 0.1% errors while returning nothing at all on 62.2% of requests. Two further traps sit on the same block: `truncated` and `tool_call_turns` are ANNOTATIONS that overlap the four states rather than extra states, so summing all six double-counts; and a tool-call turn returns zero visible characters by construction and is DELIVERED, not hollow. Trustworthiness is dated — read `outcome.measurable_from` (2026-08-13 at time of writing) and check `window_predates_measurement` rather than hard-coding the date, because a window reaching back before it yields a `delivered_rate` computed over only the classifiable rows.
references: app/services/gate/usage_aggregates.py:131 — _OUTCOME_KEYS = (failed, unknown, hollow, delivered, truncated, tool_call_turns): six keys, four states
app/services/gate/usage_aggregates.py:48 — OUTCOME_MEASURABLE_FROM = '2026-08-13'; :688 emitted as outcome.measurable_from (NOT 'outcome_measurable_from', a name that exists nowhere in the codebase)
app/services/gate/usage_aggregates.py:686 — window_predates_measurement, and delivered_rate computed over `classified`, not over `total`
